title: Dishonored director Harvey Smith thinks there's still room for big-budget immersive sims: 'When it really comes together and it has the budget behind it and the team, you end up with Deus Ex or Dishonored'
text:
Should immersive sims rein in their budgets? Thief designer Randy Smith Evergreen thinks so. We chatted to him last month, where he said a lot of immersive sims are in "an arms race to be bigger and better" , but that the size of the audience and the competition from other big-budget games makes that a mistake.
His friend and fellow immersive sim designer, Harvey Smith, has a different take. Smith recently left Arkane, where he was the director of Dishonored and co-director of Redfall, to set up his own studio, Black Pony Immersive .
"I go to get coffee with Randy every now and then, and I'm overdue for that," Smith tells us. "He's a vegetarian, so sometimes we hit one of these hippy places where you can get a black bean burger or whatever. So next time I'm together with him, I'm just gonna berate him for this opinion."
He doesn't really disagree, though. Smith Evergreen's main point was that big budgets can become a noose, one which inflates publisher expectations and forces niche immersive sims to compete with games boasting mass market appeal. And Smith agrees, you have to "right-size your budget".
Where they differ is that Smith thinks you can make an immersive sim at any scale. "If you wanted it to be a really short, two-hour experience that just models your mom's house, you could do that. On the other hand, I feel like when it really comes together and it has the budget behind it and the team, you end up with Deus Ex or Dishonored or BioShock."
But he acknowledges the risks that come with designing a money guzzler. "The thing you can't do is get so conservative with your features—which often happens the more money you're spending—[that] you don't do the fun, creative, interesting parts of immersive sims."
The blockbuster game space is undeniably conservative at times. Just look at the disappointing Wolverine, which won't be coming to PC and is no great loss. The whole experience leads you by the nose, and all you get to do is bash a single button. This simplicity is bad enough in an action game; for an immersive sim, it would be fatal.
Big imsims need to have a foundation that lets players go nuts. Smith offers an example from Deus Ex, where he was lead designer. Players used magnetic mines to climb walls, hopping onto one, then grabbing the one beneath them and placing it higher. This wasn't something the team had planned for.
(Image credit: Eidos Interactive) "That's just one example," he adds, "but tactically speaking, as you're playing, emergent stuff happens all the time because the AI is very analogue and fully featured, and the physics is very analogue and fully featured. And then you combine that with creative tools and a player who can often hide and observe, and it just becomes this explosion of possible permutations."
For smaller projects, the same risks exist, however. "The person making their own attempt at an immersive sim might not have the sort of people-power, budget or time to make a system that has as much range and as much depth," Smith says.
"If you just end up with some cool art and music and nice notes here and there, and you can walk through it, it's kind of adjacent to an immersive sim, but it's missing that sweet spot. So I think you could equally argue that going the other direction, and I know Randy knows this, you could lack some of the things that make immersive sims special."
Ultimately, the two designers end up with similar conclusions. That there is a sweet spot. "If you go too small or too large, then yeah, you probably lose something," says Smith. "Maybe it's just a nuanced way of saying what Randy Smith Evergreen, my friend, said. I love Randy. I've known him for a long time."
(Image credit: Arkane Studios) Certainly, Dishonored benefited from having a big budget, and Dishonored 2 remains the greatest immersive sim ever made. But the industry has changed. A slew of huge acquisitions have given a tiny handful of publishers all the power, and while they will gladly throw vast sums of money at a project, that comes with daunting expectations—when they aren't met, the studios suffer.
This is what happened to Smith and Arkane. Dishonored 2 was a critical darling but failed to meet Bethesda's expectations. That happened again with Prey. And then Arkane Austin ended up making Redfall , a multiplayer shooter, that resulted in the studio's death. Arkane Lyon, meanwhile, faces an uncertain future following the "Xbox reset".
So while I do get excited when I see an immersive sim that's clearly been given a lot of resources, I'm always looking for the strings.
Smith's new venture, Black Pony Immersive, hasn't announced its first game yet, but I'm excited to see what he and his team are capable of when they don't have a publisher holding an axe to their necks.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang tells Trump he agrees the AI doomsayers are perpetrating a hoax: 'you saw through all of that'
text:
There's been a lot of talk about AI 'slowdown' over the last few days, since Anthropic's CEO Dario Amodei said the industry needs to slow down to allow for better safety measures to be implemented, with these comments themselves riding in the wake of recent cybersecurity threats . Seemingly every big tech bro and even world leaders have been keen to discuss the issue.
Naturally, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom has been keen to say something on the issue and urge against slowing things down. His comments, however, were interspersed with similar sentiments from US President Donald Trump, who called the CEO while the latter was on-stage for the All-In Podcast (via CNBC ).
Huang expressed gratitude for Trump's calling AI doomsaying a hoax: "There’s a lot of complexity and the fact of the matter is you saw through all of that, and we're all just really grateful."
In a previous post on Truth Social, Trump had explained : "The only control or “guardrails” that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades! The Trump Administration has stopped AI “people” from doing bad, or potentially bad, “things,“ like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a “perfect little angel” - and we will continue to do so! We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies! There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS!"
On his call with the Nvidia CEO, he said: "I'm telling you it's all a hoax. The datacenters are great... they're just playing right into the hands of a lot of people that don't want to see it happen... We're not going to let that happen. It's a hoax."
Huang: "You're right. We're not going to let that happen, sir."
Trump: "We have to do things and we have to do it prudently, but that doesn't mean we're going to stop an industry... I didn't know how you felt about it. I assumed you felt the same way as me."
Huang again: "Yes sir... We're going to make sure that everybody wins in the AI race in America. Every industry, every company, every state, every people."
(Image credit: Bridget Bennett/Bloomberg via Getty Images (left) / GummyBone via Getty Images (right)) Perhaps as clarification or just reiteration, the president took to Truth Social to say , "I am the Hoax Buster, and I’m right now breaking another Hoax—That AI is going to take over, consume, and destroy the World, and that Robots will be marching into our Cities, and getting rid of us all!"
To my eyes and ears, all of this is a misnomer anyway. The AI boom is causing problems in the here and now, from ever-increasing energy use to ever-decreasing brain use , increasing use of AI for creative tasks that humans once enjoyed doing, and, of course, increasingly expensive tech thanks to the AI industry-induced global memory shortage , to name just a few.
Much of the actual discussion around safety and pacing AI is, of course, prudent. But my problem is with the framing of discussions in the wake of this. Talk of whether or not AI will destroy the world conveniently serves to downplay and distract from these more immediate and very real concerns . As does the idea that we (the West, and more specifically the US) are in an arms race that must be won.
If everyone is busy thinking about whether or not the AI industry could pose grand threats to national security and whether it could end society and therefore needs to slow down, nobody is busy talking about the fact that we have lots of choices over whether and how the AI industry should change society regardless. Even if AI doesn't pose a big cybersecurity threat, for instance, we should still have a choice over the potential upheaval it is causing. But without discussions centred on this, the industry rolls on regardless.

title: Blizzard finally told players where the big sword in WoW went after 8 years, and I'm just bummed out a reveal this cool was in an interview somewhere
text:
It's been a meme for eight years— where's the sword, Blizzard ? At the end of World of Warcraft : Legion, the big bad Sargeras tried to punch a big, corruptive sword into the heart of Azeroth. For years—eight years and nine months, to be exact—it's been a big, hanging question mark over the game's lore.
Especially given that, up until the Worldsoul Saga, Blizzard has been a little scattershot with its expansion ideas. The current trilogy is the company's first real, proper attempt at a multi-expansion storyline, à la Final Fantasy 14's 10-year epic that carried it from A Realm Reborn to Endwalker.
Which is why I'm a little bummed out, man. In an interview with WoWHead , associate game director Paul Kubit says that in the Midnight: What's Next recap , a screenshot of Azeroth's worldsoul with a jagged spike pointed towards it? Yeah, that's the sword. No—really, Kubit said "Yeah, yeah. That's the sword." Look:
"Yeah, yeah. That's the Sword. Eagle-eyed viewers have identified that, and yeah, we've been thinking about the Sword and it should become very apparent to people as you play through Eclipse that we haven't forgotten about the Sword. This is not something that is going away. Also, how tragically close it came to the Worldsoul is a testament to how close he came, but also maybe the power of the Worldsoul herself."
(Image credit: Blizzard) I'm bothered, somewhat, because on paper this is a super cool detail—look at that thing. It came literally feet away from punching into the centre of the world, which would've corrupted the entire planet with fel magic. Per WoW cosmology, it would've also stopped the void lords from turning it into a Dark Titan, which was kind of Sargeras' whole deal. But it also would've killed everybody, so—too many eggs for that omelette.
I'm imagining a world in which I dropped into this zone for the first time, saw that sword-tip inches away from Azeroth's soul, and went: Oh, crap. We were this close to the end of the world.
I'll keep things vague for spoiler reasons, but Final Fantasy 14—which keeps story elements under wraps before the patch or expansion they're due comes out—is really good at this. At several points in its winding 10-year story , a vista or an environment pulls double duty as part of the narrative: Like an impossible glimmering city under the ocean, or a heartachingly gorgeous faery landscape in a dying world.
But WoW doesn't do this. It tests patches for weeks on the PTR with preview cutscenes and, as mentioned above, it reveals huge overarching narrative beats during interviews and press conferences—which robs Blizzard of a pretty solid tool in its arsenal: Letting the environment show you the story.
Rather than having an "oh, shit!" moment when I saw this sword while in Midnight's final raid, and slowly piecing it together, I have instead been told in a quote by a director that I will, in a handful of months, see exactly what he said I'd see. And, listen—even though I've been impressed by some elements of Midnight's story , it's not exactly gripped my heart like FF14's did. And as long as we live in a world where big reveals like this aren't treated with much sanctity, it's probably gonna stay that way.

title: CDPR wants to make The Witcher 3 Remastered feel like any other game released today: 'It's so easy to get used to these new improvements that it's hard to go back'
text:
As if September wasn't busy enough, The Witcher 3 is calling us again . CDPR's remaster will be launching as a free update on September 29. The studio's goal with this new version is to make it feel like a 2026 game, rather than a 2015 game that's been dusted off. And while this is the second time it's had a glow up, the team has been focusing on different things.
"The next gen update a few years ago, it was quite a substantial update," executive producer Jakub Kutrzuba tells us. "At the same time, it was driven by the new generation of consoles, so there was a specific need. We wanted to bring the game to the new generation, and it was very much technical oriented." With the remaster, however, CDPR's brief has been a lot broader.
"With the remaster, it is even bigger and it's also quite heavy, maybe even heavier on the technical level," says Kutrzuba, though it should still run fine on Steam Deck . "But what is more important is that we are touching these aspects of the game which weren't touched since we launched it. I'm talking about the animation. I'm talking about the gameplay. I'm talking about the quality of life, how you actually play the game."
CDPR realised that only doing another technical update "would probably not be enough". The team wanted to make it "shine again" and give both veterans and new players an experience that wouldn't contain any "bad surprises" or anything that would make them think that The Witcher 3 got old.
"We wanted to make it [comparable] with any other game which is launching these days," says Kutrzuba.
This meant that CDPR had to change the animation system, the camera work, enemy behaviour in combat, pathfinding, and then add all sorts of small quality of life improvements. Anywhere the team identified the potential for frustration, it made changes. Anything that could be done without "rebuilding the game from scratch", basically.
Kutrzuba says the best evidence that CDPR has succeeded is that the team can't go back to the old version of the game. "It's so easy to get used to these new improvements that it's hard to go back."
I can't deny I'm excited. But also, I don't have time to play all the brand new games coming out, so I definitely won't be replaying The Witcher 3 in 2026. Next year when the new expansion arrives , though? Yeah, I'm gonna be all over that.

title: Toss a project at your printer: vibe coded tool allows developer to throw stuff at his 3D printer in VR to begin printing
text:
I trust AI about as far as I can throw it—and I'm definitely not strong enough to lift up a data centre server rack. Flinging a facsimile of the OpenAI logo around VR is a little more realistic for my weight class, and now a software developer at Epic (no, not that one) has at least in part fulfilled that vision.
Earlier this week, Hank Berger shared a short clip of himself in VR , picking up the aforementioned model from his 3D software, and hurling it to his 3D printer, where it begins printing. Berger wrote, "I've never felt more like Tony Stark than I do now."
So, yes, it's more a project borne out of AI enthusiasm rather than sharing in my scepticism. The Bambu Lab printer API allows users to control the 3D printer locally, though Berger notes in a follow up post that "Unfortunately, it makes the mobile app stop working." So, the developer "spun up a quick webserver" on his PC, and then leveraged GPT-6 Astra to get his Meta Quest 3 headset, the mobile app, and his 3D printer to all 'talk' to each other.
He shared on X that the project is "not up on GitHub yet, but I might consider it if there's enough interest," explaining that it "needs a bit more polish to be distribution ready." Berger has also posted a number of his other AI-assisted experiments in recent weeks, including completely unofficial VR ports of Luigi's Mansion and Super Smash Bros Melee .
As we've covered in the past, a number of independent developer communities have been picking apart retro games and meticulously putting them back together again so that they are playable on PC . This retro game decompilation scene has become the new AI vibe coding battleground , due to an influx of 'AI rush jobs' as our Wes describes them.
I've never felt more like Tony Stark than I do now. Using my Meta Quest, I can just throw 3D models at my 3D printers to have them start printing it😂 pic.twitter.com/xNTe4KAVM2 September 13, 2026
While Berger's VR-take on Super Smash Bros Melee is based on an 'AI accelerated' decompilation , his Luigi's Manson VR project isn't; he explains in a follow up post that "Astra can help you install an emulator and modify the ROM" to run Luigi's Mansion in VR. He also stresses "Decompiling is a very long and intensive task and will burn through your [AI subscription] usage!"
Personally, I would prefer to work out my own frustrations about the AI-induced memory crisis by donning my own VR headset— if I had any .

title: The best Total War game is getting a remaster with 50 newly playable factions, modern visuals, and a full Japanese voiceover
text:
Total War fans are eating good recently. Lovers of fantasy have the Lords of the End Times DLC for Total War: Warhammer inbound, historical fans have Medieval 3 on the distant horizon, and even enjoyers of grim dark sci-fi have Total War: Warhammer 40k likely dropping next year. Well, it gets even better.
Today, Creative Assembly announced that Total War: Shogun 2 is getting a remaster on October 13. Widely considered to be one of the best Total War games (especially its Fall of Samurai expansion) Shogun 2 originally came out in 2011, so it's starting to show its age a little bit.
Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition includes all three campaigns (Shogun 2, Rise of the Samurai, Fall of the Samurai) alongside every faction DLC which was sold piecemeal, but also a range of other improvements, including:
Full Japanese and Chinese voice and text localisation
Improved visuals, lighting and shadows
1440p and 4K UI scaling
Modernised controls
More than 50 newly playable factions
Integrated Mod.io support
64-bit upgrade
Ultrawide monitor support
Colourblind accessibility options
While I don't actually think Shogun 2 has aged as poorly as some other Total War games due to its simple visual style, its controls definitely have, so that's one thing I'm personally very excited for. There are also apparently "over 50 newly playable minor factions" in this version.
It's hard to say whether this just means all of the factions who were previously unplayable across all three campaigns, or whether it's including the factions that were sold as DLC before. Still, it's going to be a lot of content.
Those who own Shogun 2 already will receive legacy DLC from the original game at no extra cost, which I'm assuming means all of the campaigns and paid factions. Owners will also get a "75% time-limited loyalty discount" on the new edition, so not free, but all Shogun 2 players will be getting something either way.
I've got to say, I'm pretty hyped though. Shogun 2, especially Fall of the Samurai, is one of my most played Total War games. What'll be even more fun is the potential for a multiplayer revival—Shogun 2 has a feature where other players could drop into your campaign to battle against you as an enemy army, so maybe years later it'll actually have enough players to function again, not to mention the popular Avatar Conquest mode.

title: Serial numbers on RTX Founders Edition graphics cards, including PC Gamer's very own, are fading and apparently it's causing a problem with RMA requests
text:
As GPUs continue to increase in price, it also, of course, becomes increasingly important to feel that those purchases are secure from leaving you with a very expensive paperweight. This is doubly so for the RTX 5090, which now costs upwards of $5,000 . Given this, it's important that RMAs go smoothly, but judging by recent comments online, the design of the Nvidia GPUs themselves could throw a spanner in the works.
According to Redditor Willing-Avocado-4830, they recently struggled with Nvidia's RMA process for their RTX 5090 FE because of a faded serial number. They claim the RMA request was rejected. The Nvidia rep's quoted comments seem to have since been deleted or are just not visible for some reason, but the thing to highlight here is the fading itself.
If it were a lone issue, then it might not be as noteworthy, but others in the comments confirm that the serial number on their FE card has also faded—and not only RTX 5090 ones. And indeed, the serial number on our very own RTX 5080 FE, pictured above, appears to have faded somewhat. The number itself is located on the metal part of the I/O side that slots down between the case and the motherboard.
It's probably worth noting that the amount of fading on our version here at PC Gamer might be different to the home user's. We tend to swap between GPUs quite a lot for testing, which could cause more fading for us. Or, if the fading is caused by consistent heat, then it could be that the normal home use would result in more fading. Your guess is as good as mine on that front.
Serial numbers are traditionally found on stickers on the GPU, but some newer RTX FE cards have them put directly on the bottom jut of the PCIe bracket, and they seem to be prone to fading. Presumably the reason this might cause a problem with the RMA process because Nvidia will need to verify authenticity and ensure it's within warranty. And unless there's another sticker elsewhere with it on (on the PCB, for instance, or on the packaging if you still have it), that serial number can be important.
My RTX 5090 FE RMA was rejected because the physical serial number is no longer readable — has anyone experienced this?  from  r/nvidia Nvidia's warranty (in its US wording) explains : "This warranty applies only to the original purchases of the Warranted Products from a retailer, mail order operation, or on-line retail store; this warranty will not extend to any person that acquires a Warranted Product on a used basis."
As such, it will be important for Nvidia to verify that the product is, in fact, from an original purchaser.
(Image credit: Future) Looking at what is publicly available from Nvidia about its RMA process, however, it is not clear whether a serial number is required. It's also worth noting that laws surrounding RMAs can vary from country to country.
Whatever the case, if you have a still-legible serial number on your RTX FE card, it might be worth snapping a pic of it, just in case. Though I suppose it's an open question whether that would satisfy Nvidia's requirements if it's faded off the card by the time they receive it for RMA. If not, then surely there must be a better way for Nvidia to plaster those serial numbers on there.

title: The Witcher 3's story director says an ideal quest is 'constructed in such a way that the player puts the controller away, stands up, and starts walking'
text:
The Witcher 3 , being one of the best RPGs of its era, naturally has a lot of very good quests— quests with weighty, significant choices that give you pause to think. In speaking with PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens, story director Marcin Blacha says that pause is a sign that he and his team have done something right in a story choice.
"First of all, the choice has to make you think," Blacha says, "So it cannot be obvious. You cannot simply go after one of the choices by simply pressing A all the time, so that's the first thing. Second of all, in addition to having this balance, it needs to have its own gravitas. It must be serious. It must make you think about either life or humans or this particular problem or the difficulties that the characters may have right now.
"I always repeat that when you have a really big choice in The Witcher 3, it must be constructed in such a way that the player puts the controller away, stands up, and starts walking, thinking about the choice, and then goes back, and then the player picks one of the choices."
Which tracks—when I think back to the most impactful choices of the RPGs I've played, there's usually at least been a jarring, 'sit back and think' moment that's knocked me back into my chair, if not off it entirely:
"So it is about thinking," Blacha continues. "It is about making the player immersed into the game and the problems that characters have, but also saying something about either who we are or how the world works, or how difficult life can sometimes be."
In regards to the upcoming DLC, Songs of the Past , and whether it'll have any hard choices to make? "Obviously. I mean, we are not trying to avoid difficult choices, and we are not avoiding making players uncomfortable. So I can promise that you will have both in Songs of the Past, and sometimes you will regret [your choice] and you will need to load the game to repeat your choice."

title: 上线仅半年的AI短剧黑马App「VibeShort」占据全球近90个市场iOS娱乐免费榜Top10！
text:
2026 年，短剧赛道历经多轮行业变化：3 月漫剧内容迎来一波增长热潮，4 月 AI 仿真人短剧又快速崛起。在此趋势下，众多聚焦AI短剧的产品频出，AI 短剧 App「 VibeShort 」精准踩中这波风口，上线不久后便迅速在全球爆火，成为了该赛道的黑马产品。
「VibeShort」踩中AI短剧风口，上线后其App Store榜单排名持续走高
据了解，「VibeShort」由灵动象限传媒有限公司开发运营，有媒体报道，其背后操盘手为 九州文化 。另据七麦数据监测，这款 App 自 2 月上线后，其在 App Store 的榜单排名持续攀升。以美国市场为例，其在 App Store 娱乐免费榜最高达到 Top2，在应用免费榜最高冲至 Top4。截至 9 月 15 日 13 时， 该 App 在全球近 90 个国家和地区 App Store 娱乐免费榜占据 Top10，同时在近 70 个国家和地区 App Store 娱乐畅销榜占据 Top10。
「VibeShort」在美国App Store 娱乐畅销榜排名趋势
据观察，该产品的下载及收入规模也持续走高，尤其是进入七、八月份，该产品迎来爆发式增长，其下载量及收入相比 2 月均实现大幅跃升。
据悉，「VibeShort」以 AI 剧为主，同时包含少量的译制剧和海外本土真人剧。在内容分发与推荐设计上，「VibeShort」采用 AI 个性化推荐逻辑。平台会基于用户点击、播放时长、停留、追更等行为不断学习用户喜好，实现剧集题材的精准推送。 在商业化设计上，除了短剧平台常用的年订阅，「VibeShort」还采用了周订阅的模式。 从该产品的美国区App Store产品页面可以看到，该产品提供每周 19.99 美元的 Pro 会员订阅项目，以低价试用降低用户首次付费决策成本，引导用户完成初次转化。
一条反馈，提出了会员周期与更新周期的问题
从「VibeShort」美国区的 App Store 产品页面可以看到，其 8 月的版本更新文案新增了会定期上线热门短剧与独家故事。“剧库每日上新、热门剧集持续更新”，这两类内容对应两种完全不同的用户需求： 新增整部剧集，是给还没选好剧的用户增加选择；给正在连载的老剧集更新续集，才能留住等待剧情推进的追更用户。
很多用户是被某一部短剧的剧情打动才下单会员，用户判断这次会员付费值不值，很可能是看这部剧能看到第几集。即使首页不断出现新的剧集封面，也未必能替代他想看的下一集。对于按周售卖会员的连载短剧产品，这一差异可能会直接影响用户付费前的预期管理。
据观察，有用户在该产品的 Google Play 产品页面评论下提到，有一部标注全集 100 集的短剧当时仅放出 31 集，担心购买一周会员后，还需要再次付费才能继续追剧。开发者当天回应称，正在加快制作、缩短等待时间，并建议用户在等待期间观看其他故事。从这条评论可以看到一个关键问题：会员有效期可以按天计算，但短剧的内容更新节奏，不一定和会员周期同步。
同时从「VibeShort」 官方网站可以看到，其已经提供具体剧目的分集入口。例如，9 月 11 日查看《My Homeless Boyfriend Is Actually a Billionaire》，页面列出“1–30、31–39”的分组；另一部《The Serpent King's Starving Little Mate》则列到“91–101”。
虽然目前公开信息尚不足以验证 「VibeShort」 的实际新增频率，也没有证据证明其更新安排已改善留存或续费。但对于增长运营团队来说，该产品也给我们提供了一些可以参考的方向。
对于运营连载剧集、售卖周期会员的短剧团队，可以尝试优先优化这一个地方： 在剧集详情页、由该剧跳转的付费页面，清晰区分剧集总集数、当前可观看集数、连载 / 完结状态。 只有确定排期的剧集，才标注下次更新时间；更新时间尚未敲定的，也要明确告知用户。
这样的设计，能帮助用户自主判断是现在订阅，还是等剧集内容更完整之后再入手。这么做短期可能会影响即时转化，因此评估效果时，需要同时参考付费完成量、更新相关退款、客服反馈以及后续续费数据，不能只选对自己有利的一项来判断好坏。
同时短剧团队也可以先挑选少量主推连载剧集做试点，记录同一市场、同一语言版本每日实际放出的集数，对比计划更新时间与实际上线时间。同时跟踪追到最新一集用户的等待时长，以及新集上线后用户是否回来继续观看。
结语
当下AI短剧赛道热度持续攀升，产品的商业化体系也在不断迭代完善，对于短剧平台的订阅变现模式， 我们不妨多一些尝试，比如除了常规按月、年的周期进行付费订阅，也可以试用周订阅等付费模式，或许也能取得不错的效果。此外，短剧 App 开发者还可以重点关注用户评论中的真实反馈，从中捕捉用户诉求，持续优化产品体验。

title: 《007 初露锋芒》(007 First Light) 支持路径追踪与 DLSS 光线重建，《伊莫》(Aniimo) 发布支持 DLSS 4.5
text:
《007 初露锋芒》(007 First Light) 路径追踪与 DLSS 光线重建更新于 9 月 15 日上线，带来细节更丰富的光照、阴影和反射效果，让关卡与布景更具电影感、沉浸感与真实感。
9 月 15 日，《符文世界：龙之荒野》(RuneScape: Dragonwilds) 将结束抢先体验并支持 DLSS 4.5。《活性物质》(Active Matter) 正式发布，支持 DLSS 4.5 和光线追踪。9 月 16 日，《伊莫》(Aniimo) 将上线并支持 DLSS，《无人深空》(No Man’s Sky) 和 Halloween: The Game 也将升级 DLSS。
以下是全新及即将推出的 RTX 游戏详情：
● 《007 初露锋芒》(007 First Light) ：9 月 15 日，《007 初露锋芒》(007 First Light) 在支持 DLSS 4.5 超分辨率和动态多帧生成的基础上，支持路径追踪与 DLSS 4.5 光线重建。此次更新为这款电影级詹姆斯·邦德冒险游戏带来更精细的光照、阴影与反射效果。DLSS 光线重建可确保新效果呈现最佳保真度、清晰度和准确度。GeForce RTX 50 系列 GPU 上开启路径追踪和 DLSS 光线重建的推荐系统配置请查看文章。
● 《活性物质》(Active Matter) ：Gaijin Entertainment 打造的硬核军事在线 PvPvE、PvE 及 PvP 射击游戏《活性物质》(Active Matter) 于 9 月 15 日登陆 Steam，首发即支持 DLSS 4.5，包括超分辨率、光线重建和动态多帧生成。这些技术可为开启光线追踪反射和阴影效果提供充足性能。
● 《伊莫》(Aniimo) ：Pawprint Studios 打造的免费多人在线大世界捉宠RPG《伊莫》(Aniimo) 将于 9 月 16 日发布，首发支持 DLSS 超分辨率和动态多帧生成。
● 《无人深空》(No Man’s Sky) ：Hello Games 的《无人深空》(No Man’s Sky) 发行十周年，近期推出的 Cosmos 更新升级至 DLSS 4.5，支持最新超分辨率模型和最高 6 倍多帧生成。通过 NVIDIA App 的 DLSS 优设功能可开启动态多帧生成。
● 《符文世界：龙之荒野》(RuneScape: Dragonwilds) ：随着正式 v1.0 版本发布，《符文世界：龙之荒野》(RuneScape: Dragonwilds) 将结束抢先体验，为 Kuldra 的传奇画上句号。此次更新将游戏升级至 DLSS 4.5，并新增动态多帧生成，进一步提升 GeForce RTX 玩家的图像质量与性能。
● Halloween: The Game ：IllFonic 打造的 Halloween: The Game 现已推出，将 1978 年经典电影中的故事带入动态多变的 1v4 非对称多人对战和单人剧情模式中。GeForce RTX 玩家可开启 DLSS 超分辨率和帧生成，DLSS 光线重建则可增强游戏的光线追踪效果。玩家还可通过 NVIDIA App 的 DLSS 优设功能升级至 DLSS 4.5，开启超分辨率、动态多帧生成和光线重建。

title: 蚂蚁电竞750Hz助力FISSURE裂变天地3圆满收官，Legacy中国收获三连冠
text:
2026年9月13日晚，苏州高新区文体中心体育馆。在全场六千名观众的呐喊声中，Legacy以3:0的比分击败豪门战队G2，捧起FISSURE裂变天地3世界冠军奖杯。本站T1级别CS2国际赛事结束后，Legacy的全球排名已升至世界第三。
为期六天的电竞盛宴，16支来自全球各地的顶尖战队齐聚苏州，为125万美元总奖金展开激烈争夺。赛场内外，来自中国本土的高端显示器品牌——蚂蚁电竞，将国际T1级别赛事的竞技显示标准推向了新高度，作为本届赛事官方唯一指定显示器品牌，蚂蚁电竞ANT257PF以原生750Hz刷新率，为全部16支战队提供比赛及训练专用的显示设备，以极致低延迟体验为这项国际赛事全程护航。
六天鏖战， Legacy 苏州加冕
从9月8日小组赛开打，到9月13日总决赛落幕，六天高密度赛程，每一帧画面都牵动着赛场内外的神经。
巴西战队Legacy无疑是本届赛事最耀眼的存在。从小组赛开始，Legacy便保持着良好势头，整个比赛期间仅输掉两张地图。决赛面对G2，Legacy更是势如破竹，直落三图横扫对手夺冠。队内核心latto以1.31的赛事Rating荣膺MVP。这也是Legacy在中国捧起的第三座世界冠军奖杯。巴西战队在中国赛场上的统治力，成为本届裂变天地3最热议的话题之一。
从 144Hz 到 750Hz ：刷新率的每一次革命，都在重新定义竞技
近年来，随着显示器技术水平不断提升，电竞选手们也在不断突破极限。
144Hz电竞显示器的出现，让玩家第一次感受到显示器硬件为竞技带来的飞跃性变化。从60Hz时代切换到144Hz，画面更新间隔从约16.67毫秒大幅缩短至6.94毫秒——近10毫秒的延迟降低，让无数CS玩家感觉“像是在玩两款不同的游戏”。这种跨时代的体感变化，至今仍是电竞显示器发展史上最经典的升级体验。
到了360Hz时代，射击游戏玩家的体感再次迎来大幅提升。360Hz将单帧延迟压缩至2.78毫秒，让追求极致操作的玩家在急停、拉枪、瞬狙等场景中获得更精准的视觉反馈。500Hz时代，显示器延迟首次触及2毫秒关口，而今天，750Hz显示器已将单帧延迟带到1.33毫秒——一个极致接近物理极限的数字。
从60Hz到750Hz，刷新率的每一次跃升，本质上都是在不断缩短屏幕更新画面的时间间隔。而蚂蚁电竞，正是这场技术革命中走在最前面的中国品牌。
中国显示品牌走向世界的起点
与FISSURE裂变天地3的合作，是蚂蚁电竞在国际赛场推动国际大赛显示器进入750Hz时代的重要里程。
从贝尔格莱德到苏州，从TYLOO在裂变天地1上夺得中国CS2首个T1级别国际赛事冠军，到蚂蚁电竞以750Hz最高标准站上裂变天地3的舞台——中国电竞正在全方位走向世界。本次比赛的圆满结束，也是中国显示器品牌走向世界的起点。
最后，让我们再次恭喜Legacy在苏州捧杯，也感谢16支战队的选手们为全球玩家带来的极致视觉盛宴。未来，蚂蚁电竞将以更高的标准出现在更多国际大赛之中，让世界看到：中国电竞显示技术，正驱动职业选手不断突破极限。

title: 一场快闪吸引5.7万年轻人奔赴，KPL十周年线下有何魔力？
text:
8月20日至9月8日，“KPL十周年·城市巡礼快闪西安站”落地西安大悦城。预约通道开放即秒空，20天活动周期内线下累计参与人次突破5.7万，梦叽造型装置、“农友展示区”、身份小卡DIY以及限定周边等内容，吸引大量年轻人到场体验，其中不乏专程从外地赶来的粉丝。
西安站落幕后，KPL十周年系列线下活动来到厦门。9月12日，2026年KPL夏季赛决赛打响，超1.2万人入场观赛。同日，KPL奇妙日·厦门站在厦门方特旅游度假区同步开启，十周年荣耀之路快闪也落地厦门大悦城。
从电竞赛场到城市商圈，从赛事观赛到IP体验，走过十年的KPL正在继续探索电竞赛事与年轻人日常生活连接的新方式。
从“看比赛”到“为IP而来”，西安快闪让电竞走进城市商圈
随着“电竞+文旅”模式的持续发展，观众奔赴一座城的理由，正从“看一场比赛”延伸到“参与一次有关KPL的城市活动”。
西安站快闪活动现场，12只“农友”梦叽成为核心视觉符号，成都AG超玩会、佛山DRG、深圳DYG等18支战队以主题展示形式亮相。粉丝还可以通过KPL按钮打卡机领取随机纪念卡片，DIY专属“农友身份证”，并与战队、选手相关装置合影。
活动期间，打卡装置、互动区域前始终聚集着年轻人，不少粉丝举着应援物、拿着刚买到的周边拍照留念。从B1快闪区域延伸至商场回廊，都能看到前来打卡的电竞爱好者。
8月27日Fly担任一日店长期间，现场人气进一步达到高点。大悦城户外大屏、室内天幕和快闪店大屏同步进行生日应援，商场内外聚集了大量前来互动的粉丝，现场不时响起粉丝的欢呼和应援声。Fly站在快闪店内与不同方向的粉丝打招呼、比心，并与获得互动名额的粉丝碰拳、聊天。对于不少长期在线上关注赛事的粉丝而言，这一次近距离互动，让持续多年的赛事陪伴真正从屏幕走到了现实。
这背后是KPL十年来积累的赛事记忆和社群文化。梦叽形象脱胎于2024年KPL推出的“王者梦之队”IP，其不同角色对应12位热门电竞选手与教练的性格特点、粉丝昵称和赛场记忆，让原本存在于赛事直播、社交平台中的内容，转化为可以被触摸和参与的线下体验。
值得注意的是，KPL十周年系列线下活动并非简单复制同一套快闪内容，而是通过“一城一闪”的思路，让城市特色、地方传统文化以更加年轻化的方式触达新一代消费者。西安站推出“小人叽-梦之队拼图冰箱贴”等限定周边，每块拼图都加入西安城市元素，天台打卡区域也将古城风貌纳入场景设计。
在此之前，上海站推出灵感源自小笼包的"包子叽"限定周边，海口站则有"椰子叽"限定周边与环海漫游系列。电竞IP与城市文化不再是简单的视觉叠加，而是基于每座城市的在地文化基因进行差异化开发，将传统元素转化为Z世代乐于主动传播和消费的产品形态，推动文化价值与商业价值的双重落地。
从夏决到奇妙日，KPL正在与城市发生更多连接
而近期KPL刚刚在厦门结束的一系列活动更进一步放大了赛事与城市之间的连接。
9月12日，KPL王者荣耀职业联赛夏季赛总决赛在厦门落下帷幕，广州TTG与重庆狼队鏖战至巅峰对决，最终广州TTG以4：3战胜对手，捧起象征KPL最高荣誉的银龙杯，这也是广州TTG队史第二冠。
赛场内顶尖选手的对抗引发了全城狂热共鸣。决赛当日，场馆入场人数超1.2万人，省外观众占比77%。大量年轻人为电竞奔赴一座城，展现出KPL电竞赛事强大的跨城聚客效应。
与决赛正赛形成深度呼应的是，同日在厦门方特旅游度假区同步开启的“2026 KPL奇妙日·厦门站”活动，以及落地厦门大悦城的“KPL十周年·荣耀之路快闪厦门站”也吸引了数万名玩家参与。
KPL奇妙日厦门站以“康平海港”为主题，梦幻王国·梦幻奇遇港与东方神画·东方山海港两座园区共同呈现“双港口”场景，18家KPL俱乐部悉数亮相；KPL十周年快闪·厦门站空间则通过十年荣誉长廊与沉浸式互动展陈，进一步延展了粉丝打卡动线依托“场馆内高燃巅峰对抗+主题乐园沉浸游园+城市核心地标快闪”的三维联动模式，赛事期间构建起城市文旅场景融合闭环，为本地消费和城市体验带来更多人流与关注。
从这个角度看，“一城一闪”并不只是快闪活动本身的形式变化，而是KPL尝试根据不同城市的商业空间、文化特色和消费场景，对同一电竞IP进行重新组织。电竞内容与城市本身发生关系，粉丝也因此拥有了“为赛事而来”之外的更多出行理由。
在此之前，KPL十周年以"荣耀之路"与"城市巡礼"双线并行，目前已横跨九城，从海口到西安、从上海到成都，覆盖南北不同能级城市的商圈与文旅场景。这种跨地域的密集落地，验证了“一城一闪”模式在不同城市文化土壤中的快速落地能力。《王者荣耀》庞大用户基本盘与跨圈层影响力，也成为这一模式的核心壁垒之一。
从赛事配套到城市体验，KPL线下生态进入3.0阶段
回看KPL十年的线下发展，可以看到一条越来越清晰的演进路径。
早期，线下的核心是“赛场”，观众为赛事奔赴举办城市，在专业场馆中见证比赛结果；随着赛事生态发展，KPL逐渐将观赛体验拓展至更多城市和消费场景。2026年春季赛决赛期间，KPL将主题观赛空间“痛楼”带到全国30城41座影城，让更多观众能够在熟悉的城市与同好共同观赛。
如今，以“奇妙日”“城市巡礼快闪”等为代表的活动，将电竞IP放入古镇、主题乐园、商业综合体等城市生活场景，KPL的线下场景也从“赛事配套”逐渐拓展为独立的内容体验。
当王者电竞的线下活动能像音乐节、漫展一样，成为年轻人愿意主动奔赴的城市目的地，它就完成了从圈层文化到大众生活方式的跨越。
KPL“一城一闪”策略将赛事记忆、俱乐部文化和城市空间进行连接，让电竞线下体验从“观赛”变成用户愿意主动奔赴的城市内容。而随着更多城市被纳入活动版图，快闪、奇妙日等轻量化活动有望与赛事共同构成更加丰富的线下体验，让电竞成为年轻人与城市建立连接的一种新方式，也为电竞产业与文旅、商业等领域的融合创造更多可能。

title: Parent Guide to Back-to-School Screen-Time Discussions
text:
As summer vacation winds down and kids head back to the classroom, parents everywhere are managing a transition to new routines. The days of sleeping in, extra screen time, and staying up later have come to a close, and kids (and parents) are adjusting to their new reality. For many households, that means taking a closer look at online gaming and other screen-time habits.
The good news is, parents don’t need to become tech experts to guide their kids through this shift. The shift back to school hours creates a natural opportunity for parents and caregivers to discuss healthy digital routines that support sleep, homework, learning, connection, and creativity. As an expert in digital parenting and education, I’m sharing a few practical strategies that can help families set realistic routines together; without turning screen time into a battle.
1. Set new guidelines together. Parental controls for things like screen time and spending limits can be helpful digital boundaries. But these are most effective when they’re part of an ongoing conversation between parents and kids. Letting kids actively participate in these decisions helps them learn how to self-regulate and teaches them to be digitally responsible, not just digitally restricted.
Decide together how much screen time is OK and when it’s time to shut down. For example, no screens during homework time, at dinner, at bedtime. Discuss a reasonable monthly budget for in-game purchases and have them help track it, and maybe even contribute some of their own allowance or pocket money. To set a good example, parents can agree to put their screens away during agreed-upon times, as well. Then write them down somewhere visible, like the fridge, so it’s a shared agreement everyone in the household can be held to.
2. Explore their digital world with them. Instead of monitoring from the sidelines, ask kids what they’re playing and who they’re playing with when they’re online. Let them become the teacher and share the games they like. Playing together builds trust, lets parents start to understand how their kids navigate online spaces, and opens the door to continuous, nonjudgmental conversations about healthy digital behavior.
Parents of younger children can use resources like Roblox’s Family Zone , a game specifically designed to teach parents and caregivers about the games and settings available for families. For older kids, walk through their settings and give them a chance to explain what’s important to them. For example, they may want more time in the late evening because that’s when their friends are online and they want to play together.
3. Help them develop important life skills. The right time to begin discussing online safety is as soon as a child begins using technology. Discussing and setting boundaries for their digital life can be the subtext for teaching children how to manage their time and take ownership of their routines in all areas of their lives. Focus on empowering them with digital literacy, so they make smart, safe decisions even when they don’t have an adult in the room, looking over their shoulder.
Arm them with clear strategies ahead of time, so they know exactly what to do if a stranger tries to contact them in any online setting or someone asks them to move to a different site to chat. Talk about how to use reporting tools, and let them know they can come discuss it openly and make decisions together.
If they push boundaries or break the online rules that were set, approach it the same as real-life rule-breaking; with appropriate, calm consequences. Ask them why they felt they had to bypass the rules, work on a compromise together, and focus on rebuilding trust. Visit our parenting guides for more information about navigating these conversations.
4. Focus on behavior over minutes. Watch how kids act. Are they sleeping and eating well? Are they doing well in school? Are they behaving respectfully to caregivers, siblings, and teachers? Are they interacting well with friends? If all of these answers are yes, there likely is not a screen issue. The time to step in is when behavior seems to be changing. Talk to them about what’s changed and why, and decide together if online rules need to be adjusted. The guide to gaming and mental health can help them understand some of the changes they might notice in themselves or others.
5. Remember that all screen time isn’t the same. Sitting alone scrolling an endless feed is different from creating, collaborating, or playing with friends even when that’s online rather than in person. The best way to understand exactly how kids are spending their screen time (and why it’s fun for them) is a real conversation.
Gaming with friends may provide opportunities for learning, creativity, and collaboration. On Roblox, kids could be learning how to code or design or expressing themselves by trying out new looks with their avatar. As kids get older, screens may become part of their schoolwork. By taking the time to understand the different homework apps, online research, and class communications tools their kids are expected to use, parents can distinguish productive, required screen time from play or social use.
Finally, remember that kids are always learning by watching what the adults around them are doing. Adults can be aware of their own screen usage and create device-free zones and moments (e.g., no screens at the dinner table). Let kids know that adults also have to set limits and sometimes overdo it, and tell them what that feels like (headache, grumpy, etc.). That may help them recognize the signs themselves and realize when it’s time to put the device away. A new school year is a natural moment to build these habits as a family, so that the time you have together stays time you actually spend with each other.

title: 观察丨《坦克世界》2026助农行动圆满收官：200辆爱心三轮车已驶入山西两县
text:
今日，经典军武网游《坦克世界》发布了助农项目收官视频，宣告2026年度“秋收硕果，纵情驾驶”助农帮扶活动圆满落幕。视频回顾了本次活动的实施过程与落地成果，200辆农用电动三轮车已顺利交付山西省石楼县与灵丘县的农户手中，为当地农产品运输打通了“最后一公里”。
https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1XqYy6hEV6/
聚焦山区运输，精准帮扶红色县域
本次助农活动的帮扶地点选定为山西省石楼县与灵丘县。石楼县地处吕梁山区、黄河沿岸，灵丘县位于太行山区，两地因地制宜发展红枣、红薯、核桃、杂粮等特色农产品。由于当地地理环境沟壑纵横、道路崎岖，农户长期面临农产品从田间地头向村内集中点转运不便的难题。轻便灵活、结实耐用的农用电动三轮车，恰好补上了这一运输缺口。
玩家线上助力，一周达成捐赠目标
2026年度助农帮扶活动延续了2025年“心系热土 忠爱守护”助农活动玩家线上参与、官方线下落实的模式：玩家登录官网报名并完成指定游戏任务，即可推动全服助力进度条。今年的活动于8月26日上线后，在全服玩家的踊跃参与下，200辆电动三轮车的捐赠目标很快达成。
专属挂件“满载的三蹦子”成暖心纪念
为回馈参与助力的玩家，官方将捐赠给农户的电动三轮车外观制作成了游戏内的3D附件——“满载的三蹦子”。车身细节高度还原实物，参与活动的玩家均有机会获得这一极具纪念意义的奖励。
这并非《坦克世界》首次涉足助农帮扶。2025年，游戏曾为云南省金平、麻栗坡两县捐赠200辆农用电动三轮车，有效缓解了高海拔山区农产品运输难题。从云岭到太行，从虚拟战场到田间地头，《坦克世界》以“游戏+助农”的创新实践，为乡村振兴注入了一份独特的数字力量。

Apple 发布新一代 Apple Intelligence，推出全面重构的 Siri AI，支持个人语境理解、屏幕感知、系统级应用操作和跨设备对话，今日起以英文测试版随 2027 系统更新推出，下月扩展至法语、日语、韩语、葡萄牙语和西班牙语。

2027 年软件版本于今日起正式推出，为用户每天依赖的应用和体验带来 Siri AI 以及众多实用的 Apple Intelligence 智能功能

视频 · 前往原文观看

新一代 Apple Intelligence 于今日正式上线，为 Siri AI 提供支持，让用户每天依赖的应用和体验比以往更加个性化、更加实用。

Apple 今天发布了新一代 Apple Intelligence，为 Siri AI——一个全新版本的 Siri——提供支持，并带来一系列功能，让用户每天依赖的应用和体验比以往更加个性化、更加实用。Siri AI 是一个能力显著提升、可进行对话交互的智能助手，具备个人情境理解、广泛的世界知识、屏幕内容感知能力，以及更丰富的系统级应用操作。

Siri AI 能够帮助用户在需要时即时找到所需内容，从回答几乎任何主题的问题，到从用户的短信、邮件、照片等中调取相关信息。此外，Apple Intelligence 还让 Apple 产品上的日常体验更加个性化、更加实用，包括照片应用中的全新编辑功能、Safari 中的智能浏览工具，以及能够生成照片级逼真图像的全新 Image Playground 等更多功能。

随着 Apple 2027 年软件版本的发布，用户现在可以在各类应用中使用全新的 Apple Intelligence 功能。Siri AI 从今天起以测试版形式推出英文版，并将于下个月扩展到法语、日语、韩语、葡萄牙语和西班牙语。

焕然一新的 Siri

Siri AI 是彻底重新构想的 Siri 版本，更加个性化、更加强大。凭借详尽的回答和丰富自然的对话，Siri AI 帮助用户完成前所未有的更多任务。

这款新版本的 Siri 构建于 Apple Intelligence 之上，借助个人情境理解能力，帮助用户在需要时从信息、邮件、照片等应用中即时找到所需内容。凭借更丰富的系统级应用操作，Siri AI 可以帮助用户完成诸如从头撰写一封邮件或编辑并分享一组照片等任务。

凭借更丰富的系统级应用操作，Siri AI 可以帮助用户完成诸如从头撰写一封邮件等任务。

例如，如果用户询问 Siri 某位家人在即将到来的探访中提议了什么活动，Siri 可以搜索用户的信息并找到对方提到想一起烘焙一道家传食谱。随后，Siri 可以从这位亲属之前发送的邮件中调出烹饪步骤，并把所需食材添加到“提醒事项”应用中的购物清单里。

Siri AI 已经能够与 Apple 庞大开发者生态中的应用无缝协作。用户可以继续在已有应用中通过 Siri 采取操作，比如在 WhatsApp 中给朋友发信息，或在 Audible 上播放有声书。而很快，用户将能够请 Siri AI 在 Microsoft Outlook 中起草邮件、在 Notability 中搜索作业，或在 Tripsy 中添加餐厅推荐。

借助屏幕感知能力，Siri AI 可以回答问题或针对用户屏幕上的内容执行操作。例如，当用户浏览自己喜爱球队的网站时，可以让 Siri 查找所有即将进行的主场比赛，并直接添加到日历中。此外，Siri AI 还能利用广泛的世界知识，获取几乎所有主题的最新信息。无论是查询足球比赛的比分、寻找度假规划的建议，还是想在新城市找到最好的本地咖啡店，Siri AI 都会利用来自全网的信息，提供有用且准确的答案。

借助屏幕感知能力，Siri AI 可以回答问题或针对用户屏幕上的内容执行操作。

用户几乎可以将 Siri 的任何回复延伸为丰富的对话，并追问后续问题。而且用户可以在系统的任何地方使用 Siri AI。除了说“Hey Siri”之外，iPhone 用户还可以通过侧边按钮唤起 Siri，或从灵动岛向下滑动来开启对话并获得深入的回答。

在 iPad 和 Mac 上，Siri AI 已集成到 Spotlight 中，用户可以搜索几乎所有问题的答案。它还集成到了系统全局的上下文菜单中，用户只需按住 Control 键点击，即可询问屏幕上的图片、文件或文本。

在 Apple Vision Pro 上，Siri AI 借助空间计算提供 3D 可视化界面，用户可以将其放置在空间中的任意位置，只需注视它并开口说话即可唤起 Siri。

如需回顾过去的对话或开启新对话，用户可以打开全新的专属 Siri 应用。

Siri 应用利用 iCloud 在用户的各设备间私密同步对话历史，因此用户可以在 iPhone 上开始与 Siri 对话，然后在 Mac、iPad、Apple Watch 或 Apple Vision Pro 上继续这段对话，将丰富的对话汇聚在一处。

当用户想要回顾过去的对话或开启新对话时，可以打开全新的专用 Siri 应用。
由最先进的端侧模型驱动的富有表现力的语音和改进的听写功能

Siri AI 提供更加富有表现力的语音，并大幅提升准确度，为支持 Apple 迄今最先进的端侧模型 AFM Core Advanced 的产品提供系统级听写功能。

用户可以自定义 Siri 语音的表现力和语速，使之恰到好处。听写功能现在能以更高的精度将用户所说的话转化为润色后的文本，在用户说话时自动处理大小写、标点和格式。凭借改进的语音理解能力，用户可以自然地说话，并相信自己的话语会清晰、准确、如预期地呈现出来。

视频 · 前往原文观看

用户可以自定义 Siri 语音的表现力和语速，使之恰到好处。

视觉智能现已登陆 iPad、Mac 和 Apple Vision Pro

借助视觉智能（Visual Intelligence），Siri AI 提供强大的图像理解与多模态能力，用户可以在 iPhone、iPad、Mac 和 Apple Vision Pro 上就视觉内容提问。

在 iPhone 上，Siri 的多模态能力通过全新的 Siri 模式直接集成到相机 App 中，用户可以就眼前的事物获取信息并采取行动。例如，当看到一张音乐节海报时，用户可以询问 Siri 自己喜爱艺人的演出时间，然后让 Siri 自动为这个周末创建多个日历事件。

在 iPad 上，视觉智能直接集成到截屏体验中。在 Mac 上，用户可以通过一个专属键盘快捷键调用它，选中 Mac 屏幕上的内容并直接向 Siri 输入问题，从而获得有用的答案。视觉智能还扩展到了 Apple Vision Pro，用户只需注视某个东西就能向 Siri 提问，无论是 App 窗口内的内容，还是周围的实物。

借助 Siri AI 在几乎任何地方进行写作与编辑

Siri 现在提供比以往更强大的集成写作工具，让用户在几乎任何能输入文字的地方都可以用 Siri AI 进行写作。用户只需描述自己的需求，Siri 就能从零开始生成草稿，帮助打开思路。如果用户想润色已写的内容，只需描述想要做出的修改，Siri 就能快速更新。

集成写作工具比以往更加强大，让用户在几乎任何能输入文字的地方都可以用 Siri AI 进行写作。

在“邮件”和“信息”中书写时，Siri 能够贴合用户与每位收件人通常的沟通方式，包括他们习惯使用的标点和语气。用户可以请 Siri 提供技巧和建议，改进自己的书面内容。此外，Apple Intelligence 现在会在用户全系统输入时自动校对，包括大多数第三方应用。

Apple Intelligence 现在会在用户全系统输入时自动校对，包括大多数第三方应用。
强大的 AI 能力融入日常体验

除了 Siri AI 之外，Apple Intelligence 还为用户每天使用的应用带来更多新功能：

“照片”应用借助更强大的图像模型，提供了编辑照片的新方式，同时依然尊重拍摄时的原始瞬间。通过空间重构（Spatial Reframing），用户可以在拍摄后调整镜头视角，改善照片构图。用户还可以使用“延展”工具扩展画面，为拍摄主体留出更多空间；备受欢迎的“清理”工具也比以往更强大，让用户以更好的画质和更逼真的填充效果移除照片中的干扰元素。
依托一个在 Private Cloud Compute 上运行的新型生成式模型，Image Playground 比以往任何时候都更强大、更实用，让用户能够以几乎任何风格创建高质量图像——现在还包括照片级写实风格——并且只需描述想要的改动即可完成修改。这一能力还延伸到全新 Siri：用户只需在由 Image Playground 驱动的 Siri AI 应用中描述画面，就能生成图像。随着即将支持的 SynthID 标准，用户可以识别使用 Apple Intelligence 驱动工具生成或编辑过的图像。3
Safari 新增了多项工具，彻底改变用户浏览网页的方式。现在，Safari 可以自动将用户的标签页按主题整理归类，简化浏览体验。它还能通过“Notify Me”功能通知用户网站的变化，例如商品补货或降价，并可根据用户的描述创建自定义扩展。
在邮件和信息中，智能回复可以借鉴用户的个性化写作风格，而邮件中的建议功能也更为强大，能够通过第三方应用执行操作。
借助电话中的通话上下文（Call Context）功能，用户在致电商家时可以主动获取相关信息，例如验证码或预订号码。
在日历中，用户现在只需简单的描述即可添加或修改日程。
快捷指令比以往任何时候都更容易上手。借助描述快捷指令的功能，用户只需描述自己想要什么，即可创建复杂的自动化流程。
家庭App 新增了将相关通知理解为单一活动的能力，可通过生成的视频描述查看一系列视频片段中的动态，跨多个摄像头搜索片段，并将值得关注的片段置顶显示在搜索页面顶部。4
将于今年晚些时候推出：全新音频智能与健康功能
由于 Apple Watch 始终佩戴在用户手腕上，它是帮助用户留意重要声音、并全天保持专注投入对话的完美设备。凭借内置麦克风、S11 芯片的强大性能、iPhone 上最新的 Apple Intelligence 模型以及 Private Cloud Compute，Apple Watch Series 12 和 Apple Watch Ultra 4 带来了一类全新的 Apple Intelligence 功能。Audio Intelligence 帮助用户了解周围的世界、不错过遗漏的信息、记住关键时刻——其设计始终以用户控制、隐私、安全和无障碍为核心。5

Audio Intelligence 功能包括：

声音识别，该功能登陆 Apple Watch，可在 iPhone 不在身边时提醒听障或听力受损用户注意重要声音。此功能会监听警报声、闹钟、门铃或婴儿啼哭等声音，并利用端侧智能在检测到这些声音时通知用户。6
实时回放，可帮助用户回忆对话中刚刚说过的内容。双击数码表冠即可将前 15 秒的对话以文字片段形式显示，让用户能够补上可能错过或不熟悉的内容。用户可以向 Siri 询问文字内容，或将其保存到 Siri 应用中以便日后查看。7
Siri 回顾，可为对话生成高层摘要，供用户日后查看以唤起记忆。开启 Siri 回顾后，对话结束后 Apple Intelligence 会在全新的 Siri 应用中自动生成标题和要点，让用户能更专注、更投入地活在当下。8
Shazam，可即时识别用户周围正在播放的音乐，并自动在智能叠层的音乐识别小组件中显示歌曲名和艺人名，抬腕即可轻松一览。9

Audio Intelligence 功能在设计上即以隐私为先，通过硬件、软件与服务的结合，以只有 Apple 才能做到的方式保护用户隐私。这些功能不会创建或存储任何录音，用于处理的原始音频对操作系统、App、用户乃至 Apple 都完全不可访问。

这是因为 Apple Watch Series 12 和 Apple Watch Ultra 4 上的 S11 芯片包含 Secure Exclave——一个专用的硬件隔离隔间，可在与系统其余部分完全隔离的情况下处理音频，并随即立即将其删除。

用户拥有掌控权，可以选择是否启用每项 Audio Intelligence 功能。他们可以决定 Siri Recap 在何时何地记笔记，并可随时在控制中心直接开启或关闭 Siri Recap。

Audio Intelligence 功能在设计上不会识别和归属说话人身份，以保护用户及其周围人员的隐私。Siri Recap 生成的是简短、高层次的对话摘要——而非逐字记录——并且设计上会排除财务信息或政府分配标识符等敏感信息。Live Rewind 在使用时会发出可听见的提示音，即使 Apple Watch 处于静音状态也会如此，并显示全屏动画和麦克风指示符，让附近的人能够听到和看到该功能已被激活。

Live Rewind 文本片段和 Siri Recap 摘要在 Siri App 中通过 iCloud 同步时采用端到端加密，即使是 Apple 也无法访问。

进一步了解

Audio Intelligence 如何保护隐私。Siri Recap 和 Live Rewind 将于今年晚些时候以测试版形式推出。

此外，

健康 App

迎来全新设计，以 Apple Intelligence 为核心，将用户的各项指标转化为个性化指导。全新的“洞察”标签页包含由 Apple Intelligence 生成的摘要，突出显示用户最及时的信息，呈现诸如最新睡眠状况或峰值 VO2

max 等细节。用户还将从健康 App 获得个性化指导。例如，如果他们正在努力改善心血管健康，可能会看到在日常晨跑中加入间歇训练的建议——这些建议会根据用户及其数据动态调整。

全新的健康功能将于今年晚些时候推出。

大胆的架构，隐私优先

这些全新功能由下一代 Apple Foundation Models 提供支持，该模型是与 Google 及其 Gemini 模型合作定制构建的，旨在打造深度集成的 Apple Intelligence 体验。这些最新模型在设备端和使用 Private Cloud Compute 的服务器上运行。

全新 Apple Intelligence 架构的方方面面都以隐私优先为原则，从最新的 Apple Foundation Models 到将这些模型深度整合进 Apple 平台的核心操作系统技术。

Apple Intelligence 通过设备端处理和 Private Cloud Compute 帮助保护用户隐私。Private Cloud Compute 让用户能够获得前沿级别的智能，同时将 iPhone 的隐私与安全性延伸到云端。当 Private Cloud Compute 处理用户的请求时，用户的个人数据不会被存储，也不会被 Apple 或任何其他人访问。外部专家可以随时继续验证这一隐私承诺。

Siri 从底层彻底重构，搭载了强大的 AI，充分利用了 Apple Intelligence 崭新的大胆架构。此外，Siri AI 使用系统编排器调用核心能力，例如 Spotlight 索引和 App Toolbox，这些能力完全在设备端运行，让用户始终掌控自己的数据。

凭借强大的新功能和无与伦比的隐私保护，Siri 仍然是世界上最注重隐私的数字助理，其背后的大胆架构让 Apple 能够在以隐私与安全为核心的前提下推出创新的新功能。

价格与上市信息

iOS 27、iPadOS 27、macOS 27、watchOS 27 和 visionOS 27 中的 Apple Intelligence 适用于 iPhone 16 机型及更新机型、iPhone 15 Pro、iPhone 15 Pro Max、iPad mini（A17 Pro）、搭载 M1 或更新芯片的 iPad 机型、MacBook Neo（A18 Pro）、搭载 M1 或更新芯片的 Mac 机型、Apple Vision Pro、Apple Watch Series 9 及更新机型、Apple Watch Ultra 2 及更新机型，以及在附近配有支持 Apple Intelligence 的 iPhone 的情况下使用的 Apple Watch SE 3。
Apple Intelligence 支持在 Siri 设置和设备语言设为简体中文、繁体中文、丹麦语、荷兰语、英语、法语、德语、意大利语、日语、韩语、挪威语、葡萄牙语、西班牙语、瑞典语、土耳其语或越南语时使用。部分功能可能并非在所有地区或语言中均可用。部分设备可能并非在所有地区均有售。
Siri AI 正以测试版形式随 iOS 27、iPadOS 27、macOS 27、watchOS 27 和 visionOS 27 推出英语支持，并需要一台支持 Apple Intelligence 且设置为受支持语言的设备。法语、日语、韩语、葡萄牙语和西班牙语的支持将于下月推出。
Siri AI 初期将不会在欧盟的 iOS、iPadOS 和 watchOS 上提供。依赖 Siri AI 的功能在欧盟的 iOS、iPadOS 和 watchOS 上同样无法使用。Apple 正努力寻找一条既能推进又能保护用户隐私与安全的可行路径。
在 Apple 处理相关监管要求期间，Siri AI 及其他全新 Apple Intelligence 功能将不会在中国推出。
某些依赖服务器端模型的 Apple Intelligence 功能受每日使用额度限制，包括但不限于 Siri AI、智能照片编辑工具、Image Playground，以及快捷指令中的 AFM 3 Cloud 模型。每日额度可能因功能、请求复杂度、系统需求、系统策略及其他因素而有所不同。未来将提供付费的扩展使用方式。这些功能的使用须遵守 Apple Intelligence 条款与条件。了解更多信息，请访问 apple.com/apple-intelligence。
Siri AI 不向 13 岁以下的用户开放。
Apple 最强大的端侧模型及其支持的功能，如富有表现力的语音和更先进的听写，可在 iPhone Duo、iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone 18 Pro Max、iPhone Air、iPhone 17 Pro、iPhone 17 Pro Max、配备至少 12GB 统一内存的 iPad（M4）或后续机型，以及配备至少 12GB 统一内存的 Mac（M3）或后续机型上使用。该模型和富有表现力的语音也可在 Apple Vision Pro（M5）上使用。
SynthID 将于今年晚些时候通过软件更新推出，并将包含在大多数经过编辑的图像中，具体取决于所应用的编辑。
需要家庭中枢，如 HomePod（第二代）、HomePod mini 或运行最新操作系统软件的 Apple TV 4K。家庭的拥有者必须拥有支持 Apple Intelligence 的 iPhone，并在“家庭”App 中启用 Apple Intelligence，同时订阅符合条件的 iCloud+ 方案。
Audio Intelligence 包括 Live Rewind、Siri Recap、声音识别和更快的 Shazam，并需要 Apple Watch Series 12 或 Apple Watch Ultra 4。Live Rewind 和 Siri Recap 将于 2026 年底以测试版形式推出，并需要支持 Apple Intelligence 的 iPhone 16 或后续机型（不包括 iPhone 16e）。它们最初将以英语提供，且初期不在欧盟提供。某些依赖服务器端模型的 Audio Intelligence 功能受每日使用限额约束，包括但不限于 Live Rewind 和 Siri Recap。欲了解更多信息，请访问 support.apple.com/148354。
声音识别需要 Apple Watch Series 12 或 Apple Watch Ultra 4。
Live Rewind 将于 2026 年末以测试版形式推出，需要 Apple Watch Series 12 或 Apple Watch Ultra 4，并配对支持 Apple Intelligence 的 iPhone 16 或更新机型（不包括 iPhone 16e）。初期将仅提供英语版本，且初期不会在欧盟推出。某些依赖服务器端模型的音频智能（Audio Intelligence）功能受每日使用限制，包括但不限于 Live Rewind 和 Siri Recap。欲了解更多信息，请访问 support.apple.com/148354。
Siri Recap 将于 2026 年末以测试版形式推出，需要 Apple Watch Series 12 或 Apple Watch Ultra 4，并配对支持 Apple Intelligence 的 iPhone 16 或更新机型（不包括 iPhone 16e）。初期将仅提供英语版本。Siri Recap 初期不会在欧盟推出。某些依赖服务器端模型的音频智能（Audio Intelligence）功能受每日使用限制，包括但不限于 Live Rewind 和 Siri Recap。欲了解更多信息，请访问 support.apple.com/148354。
更快的 Shazam 需要 Apple Watch Series 12 或 Apple Watch Ultra 4。
重新设计的健康 App 可在支持 Apple Intelligence 的 iPhone 和 iPad 机型上配合最新软件使用，部分功能仅在 iPhone 上可用。某些功能可能并非在所有地区或语言中均可用。健康年龄（Health Age）功能需要 Apple Watch。估算最大摄氧量（VO2 max）的测试需要 Apple Watch、AirPods Pro 3 或第三方心率传感设备。某些功能要求用户年满 18 岁。有关 Apple Intelligence 可用性的信息，请访问 support.apple.com/en-us/121115。

科技巨头放缓 AI 开发的口头协议是安全共识还是卡特尔
The Verge：AI（RSS）
·
2026-09-15 06:59
·
1天前
·
Hayden Field
AI 导读

Sam Altman、Dario Amodei、Demis Hassabis 和 Elon Musk 周末粗略同意放慢 AI 开发，提出引入第三方审计、监管国内实验室并达成全球放缓协议，批评者则称其为压制竞争者和开源运动的“卡特尔”。

推荐理由

文章汇集安全研究者、监管团体与前官员的多方观点，既讨论放慢协议的价值，也剖析安全洗白与监管真空的可能走向。

标签
现象/趋势
正文 · AI 翻译
中文
原文

当 OpenAI CEO Sam Altman、Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei、Google DeepMind 联合创始人 Demis Hassabis 以及 SpaceX 负责人 Elon Musk 在周末大致同意放缓 AI 发展时，怀疑者立刻察觉到了别有用心的动机。

这些 AI 巨头宣称，他们的目标是“为前沿发展定速”，至少部分支持了一项提案，内容包括引入第三方审计机构、监管国内实验室，以及达成一项全球放缓协议。然而，批评者认为，他们只是想阻止潜在竞争者、削弱开源运动，并规避真正的法律保障——一些人直接将其称为“卡特尔”。

  据业内多方消息源称，真相更为复杂。Amodei 在一篇文章中提出的三步提案，呼吁进行 AI 安全倡导者长期主张的变革。尽管它可能成为监管的替代品，但在特朗普治下，实质性监管本来就不太可能。但专家表示，在一个只会愈发重要的问题上，AI 领导者并不是引领这场行动的最佳人选。“

整个行业需要新的领军者，”纽约大学兼职教授、美国国土安全部前新兴技术政策主管 Nick Reese 表示。“我们一直把 Dario Amodei、Sam Altman 和 Elon Musk 这样的人视为最接近问题、每天都在为此工作的人，认为他们最了解情况。

但事实是，对于我们要建设的目标，从来就没有过一个现实的愿景。”对 AI 进展的担忧已持续升级数月，主要导火索是有关大批智能体在领先前沿实验室 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 眼皮底下发动恶意黑客攻击的披露。两家公司发布的报告火上浇油，Anthropic 研究员 Jacob Coxon 的辞职同样如此，他发布了一封公开信解释自己的选择。“

构建 AI 的人真心相信，它可能在这个十年结束前杀死我们所有人，”他写道，并补充说 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 都没有“负责任地行事”，而是“径直冲向可自我改进的超级智能，拿我们的生命赌博”。在业内，关于 AI 的可怕警告并不新鲜，但 Coxon 的这封信似乎突破了圈层。

仅在 X 上，它就被浏览了超过 1.7 亿次，而 Coxon 和他的故事也登上了报纸和电视。 然而，对相当一部分 AI 安全研究人员和 AI 非营利组织工作者来说，这不过是在让一个早已被广泛讨论的问题获得更多关注。“

很多人把这当成 Dario 的想法，或者认为它来自那些 CEO，但这是错的，”前 OpenAI 员工、现领导 AI 研究非营利组织 AI Futures Project 的 Daniel Kokotajlo 说。“公司之外的人多年来一直在呼吁这件事……一直有越来越多人齐声说，‘请不要这么快就构建超级智能。

我们还没准备好。你们需要慢下来。’”Kokotajlo 说，在人们多年“冲他们喊话要求这么做”之后——包括超过 1,000 名 AI 实验室员工签署了 7 月的一封公开信，该信在 OpenAI-Hugging Face 事件后呼吁放缓 AI 开发——这些 CEO 现在“是在屈从于这种压力，同时还把功劳揽到自己身上，[尽管]这并不正当。”

 总体而言，少数消息人士告诉 The Verge，他们认为这些 AI 领导者达成的口头协议是朝着正确方向迈出的一步。NYU 的 Reese 说，他“不认为这全是空话”。Apollo Research CEO Marius Hobbhahn 称这是“一个好主意”，并表示“如果它真的发生，那会是长期以来对安全最有利的事情之一”。

The Midas Project 的 Tyler Johnston 说这是一个“好迹象”。Redwood Research CEO Buck Shlegeris 说这是“一些好消息——显然很难知道这是否会转化为任何真实的东西，但我感到谨慎乐观。””

不过，所有人都同意，要让这一口头承诺成为现实，仍有大量工作要做，尤其是在使其成为一项铁板钉钉的协议方面。许多人仍然质疑 AI 领导者的动机。长期以来，规模更大的科技行业一直通过游说制定自己偏好的规则或承诺自我监管来抢在监管之前行动。

大型平台提出的政策可能会对较小的竞争对手造成更沉重的打击，并用利他主义的言辞来为自私自利的目标辩护。它们被指责进行“安全粉饰”，即做出毫无意义的改变，给人以拥有实际安全保障的虚假印象。人们担心这种情况也会在 AI 行业发生，这并不令人意外，尤其是因为 AI 实验室的自愿安全框架多年来一直受到批评。

多位消息人士认为，对“安全粉饰”的担忧是有道理的。“有一个严重的担忧，那就是他们实际上并不会放慢脚步，”Kokotajlo 说，并补充说，令人担心的是“他们只会引入一些外部审计人员，做一堆安全文书工作——其中一些确实是有益的——但归根结底，这实际上根本不会让他们放慢多少。”

纽约大学的 Reese 将这一策略比作十年前社交媒体平台的套路，当时这些公司开始呼吁采取监管行动，以抢在即将到来、对其更不利的法律之前。Reese 说，对于 AI 行业而言，“这把锤子可能不会在本届政府任期内落下，但我认为，如果下一次选举后出现一个民主党政府，那将非常有可能。”

  Tech Oversight Project 执行董事 Sacha Haworth 表示，那种监管将至关重要。她说，任何自愿框架本质上都是监管俘获，“我们不应该让狐狸来管理鸡舍。这不是国会再次将责任外包给行业的机会。”

Political Integrity Project 联合创始人 Daniel Lobo-Lewis 表示，自愿监管很可能会重蹈 Meta 那个基本上没有牙齿的 Oversight Board 的覆辙。然而，大多数人同时也认为，除了 AI 实验室在特朗普政府执政期间已同意遵守的模型发布前审查期之外，各公司目前并无迫在眉睫的监管风险。

特朗普总统周一发帖称：“AI 唯一需要的控制或‘护栏’，就是一位强大而聪明（高智商！）的总统，而美国恰恰拥有这样一位，而且绰绰有余！”他还在 Nvidia CEO 黄仁勋出席一场会议登台时给他打了电话——特朗普通过免提对现场观众说，近期对 AI 的担忧是一场“骗局”，并且“机器人不会接管世界”。

至于监管可能拖累其他公司或开源开发者的担忧，多位行业专家对 The Verge 表示，要求放缓的呼声几乎完全针对那些以精确规模指标界定的大型前沿 AI 实验室。在政府 AI 监管迟迟未至的情况下，最好的选择或许是推动各公司达成一项即时、可衡量且可执行的协议。

例如，Kokotajlo 的 AI Futures Project 提议，AI 实验室应允许审计人员访问其算力预算——并承诺大幅削减用于研究的算力预算，从而减缓 AI 的进展，让其他 AI 实验室得以追赶。（Amodei 的文章已经呼吁 AI 实验室允许外部第三方审计机构——如 METR、Apollo 和 Redwood Research——在一定程度上嵌入其组织内部，并有可能标记和举报有问题的发现。）

可以说，AI 放缓面临的最大单一挑战可以用一个词概括：中国。  AI 领导人和政客长期以来一直将中国定位为美国 AI 进展不能放缓的理由——因为无论这项技术可能变得多么危险，他们宁愿它掌握在美国手中而非中国手中，而中国不会踩刹车。

Lobo-Lewis 将这种对中国的恐惧比作冷战时期的导弹差距。一位 X 用户写道：“如果我注定要死于杀人 AI 之手，我希望它是美国的，而不是中国的。” Redwood Research 的 Shlegeris 表示，以“鲁莽”的方式推进 AI 发展，既不符合美国也不符合中国政府的最大利益，并补充说“这并非没有先例的国际协调水平。”

Johnston 说：“（人们）想当然地认为中国不会合作”，并补充道，“这个问题如此严重、如此广泛，协调解决它似乎符合所有人的利益，就像协调核不扩散符合美国和俄罗斯双方的利益一样。”周一，中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆确实对放缓的呼吁进行了反驳，称其为“散布恐慌”。

Midas Project 的 Johnston 和 Redwood Research 的 Shlegeris 都表示，即使没有中国的合作，鼓励美国进行协调仍然至关重要。而对于 Tech Oversight Project 的 Haworth 来说，放缓是一个“将自己定位为 AI 技术如何开发和使用的指南针”的机会。

她认为反对的论调是熟悉套路的一部分。“每当一个行业想要逃避监管时，中国就会被拿出来当替罪羊。”Kokotajlo 则把这种情况比作他看到过的一个卡通画面：人们坐在一辆驶下悬崖的车里。他回忆说，那个对话气泡里写着类似“万岁，我们领先中国了”的话。

最近所有这些恐慌背后的问题是一个被称为递归自我改进的里程碑，而根据该行业当前的轨迹，我们听到的只是警报声的开始。RSI 指的是一个潜在的行业里程碑，届时 AI 模型可以训练、进步并创建自身的新版本——全程无需人类参与。Anthropic 曾表示这一时点最早可能在 2027 年初到来，而 OpenAI 的首席科学家本月早些时候写道，OpenAI 正在投入大量资源以实现这一目标。

AI 行业越来越多的工程师和研究人员担心，RSI 会先于一系列全新且更严重的 AI 隐患到来，其中包括对社会整体造成更深远影响的更严重网络安全事件。Amodei 将 RSI 列为促使他呼吁放缓的主要因素：“大约从今年夏天开始，AI 的推进速度急剧加快”，而 RSI “正开始在整个行业中出现，包括在 Anthropic……如果不加约束，它可能超出我们理解和控制系统能力的速度，因此即便要推进，也必须极其谨慎，”他在最近的文章中写道。

他提议对 RSI 的速率实施“某种‘限速’”，并将其比作对导弹数量的上限。  在 Jacob Coxon 从 Anthropic 的辞职帖中，他警告会出现“能够入侵任何东西、在一夜之间颠覆任何领域、并获取真正权力与资源的超人系统”。

领先 AI 实验室的许多其他研究人员也呼应了他的担忧。OpenAI 研究员 Jasmine Wang 写道，加速冲向 RSI 的危险程度“怎么强调都不为过”。前 Google DeepMind 员工 Vishal Maini 表示，RSI “如今已迫在眉睫，以至于其他任何选项都不合理。”

  对 RSI 的恐惧很容易演变为末日式的想象。“AI 开发者相信他们的技术可能导致人类灭绝（或类似糟糕的结果），”Anthropic 研究员 Samuel Marks 在 X 上写道，“这可能在未来几年内发生。

总体而言，员工越资深，就越担忧。”另一位 Anthropic 研究员兼团队负责人 Evan Hubinger 在 X 上写道，“Jacob 在这里说得对——我们确实真心相信 AI 可能杀死全人类！”（他给出的未来十年内发生概率高于 10%。）

前 Google DeepMind 员工 Alex Turner 写道，“许多研究人员相信他们正在构建某种可能杀死地球上所有人的东西。思考如何阻止这件事，字面意义上就是我的日常工作。” OpenAI 研究员 Micah Carroll 写道，Coxon 的看法是一种“跨党派立场”，在“所有前沿 AI 公司”的研究团队中都存在，而且他们都认为“一切照旧的 AI 开发会带来不可接受的灾难性风险”。

“但是，”Carroll 补充道，“我们也不应把灾难性风险凭空臆想成现实——通过有牙齿的安全要求、国际协调，以及一项共识：除非有足够的安全进展让我们集体确信可以这么做，否则就不构建[人工超级智能]，这些风险是可以被大幅降低的。”

这种“国际协调”正是 AI 领袖以及广大公众如今所呼吁的。 “我们从未处于这样一种境地：我们真正理解自己在 AI 方面正朝着什么方向前进，”纽约大学的 Reese 说。“我们一直都有这种模糊而未定义、我们并不真正理解、却必须击败中国才能抵达的终局状态。

当我们甚至不理解路径，甚至不理解终点线是什么——甚至不确定是否存在终点线时，真的很难去竞赛。”

推荐理由

Vercel COO 给出自家 inbound 销售自动化的人员压缩、年度基础设施成本和 32x ROI 数字，是可直接参考的一手落地案例。

标签
智能体
大佬观点
正文 · AI 翻译
中文
原文

Vercel 将其入站销售开发团队从 10 人缩减到了 1.25 人。

Jeanne DeWitt Grosser，Vercel 的 COO，在我们共同参与的 Information 采访中分享了这一点1：

“我们的入站销售开发实现了 90% 的自动化。而我们自研的支持智能体处理了所有支持工单中的 93%……

在这两种情况下，全年基础设施总账单仅为个位数千美元……

我们的销售开发智能体实现了 32 倍的投资回报率。所以无论那个模型花多少钱，这都是值得的……

我们现在有很多方式让 AI 在 99% 的时间里达到第 99 百分位的表现。”

销售开发是早期 AI 最直接的用例之一。

就像自动驾驶汽车一样，承诺已经到来，但兑现还需要更多时间，直到 Waymo 能够在 Inner Sunset 的街道上行驶。巧合的是，Waymo 将行人碰撞事故减少了 92%，与上面的数字几乎完全一致2。

如今，AI 已经处在一个最初的承诺得以兑现的阶段。

10 月 1 日星期四太平洋时间上午 11:00，Theory Office Hours 将邀请 Vercel 的 Jeanne DeWitt Grosser，探讨当 inbound 智能体自行管理线索时，销售开发职能会发生什么变化。如果你想参加，请在此注册。

Jeanne DeWitt Grosser 做客 The Information 的 TITV。关于 10→1.25 压缩的详细信息，来自 SaaStrAI 对同一场会议的报道。↩︎

Waymo，新研究：Waymo 正在减少严重碰撞事故，让最易受伤害群体的街道更安全，2025 年 5 月 1 日。该研究报告称，涉及行人的伤害事故减少了 92%，骑自行车者和摩托车骑手的事故减少了 82%。↩︎

推荐理由

原文给出语音到语音模型的完整分数、速度和成本对比，读者可据此在不同后端配置间做选型判断。

标签
OpenAI

正文 · AI 翻译
中文
原文

OpenAI 的 GPT-Live-1 首次亮相便以 81.5 分登顶 Artificial Analysis 语音到语音指数，其委托后端模型为 Astra，领先于 Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0

GPT-Live-1 是 @OpenAI 推出的全新全双工语音到语音模型，它可以将推理和工具调用委托给后端文本模型，同时继续对话。开发者通过 API 流式输入音频并接收语音返回，后端文本模型可单独配置。我们评估了两种后端配置：Astra 在中等推理强度下，以及 Sol 在低推理强度下。

关键要点： ➤ 语音到语音指数：GPT-Live-1（Astra，medium）达到 81.5，排名第 1，而 GPT-Live-1（Sol，low）得分为 80.1，排名第 3。Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 High 以 81.3 位居两者之间 ➤ 语音智能体竞技场：GPT-Live-1（Sol，low）以 1，053 Elo 在偏好度上排名第 3，任务成功率为 90.9%，而 GPT-Live-1（Astra，medium）以 1，048 Elo 排名第 4，任务成功率为 87.4%。Gemini 3.1 Flash Live Minimal 以 1，096 Elo 在偏好度上领先，而 Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 High 以 94.6% 在任务成功率上领先 ➤ Tau Voice：GPT-Live-1（Astra，medium）和 GPT-Live-1（Sol，low）在我们的智能体性能基准上占据前两名，分别为 67.9% 和 59.3%，领先于 Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 High 的 56.5%。 ➤ Big Bench Audio：GPT-Live-1（Astra，medium）得分为 90.1%，GPT-Live-1（Sol，low）得分为 89.0%，在音频推理上落后于 Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 High 的 97.2% 和 Qwen Audio 3.0 Realtime Plus 的 99.2% ➤ 速度：在 Big Bench Audio 上，GPT-Live-1（Astra，medium）的平均首次音频时间为 1.34 秒，GPT-Live-1（Sol，low）为 1.24 秒，而 Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 High 为 0.70 秒 ➤ 成本：GPT-Live-1（Astra，medium）每小时输入音频成本为 $5.83，而 GPT-Live-1（Sol，low）为 $4.47，包含委托后端模型使用量，相比之下，在我们固定的 Big Bench Audio 定价子集上，Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 High 为 $4.80

Anthropic 与 OpenAI 提议协调放缓前沿 AI 开发，Cohere CEO 等批评者质疑其真实动机

·

·

·
Matthias Bastian
AI 导读

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 呼吁行业与政府协调放缓前沿 AI 开发，并寻求反垄断豁免，Sam Altman 与 Elon Musk 表示同意。

推荐理由

文章汇总了各方对头部 AI 实验室提议放缓前沿模型开发的批评与政治反应，呈现了安全叙事之外的竞争与监管分歧。

本文目录
要点
Cohere CEO 称其为“换了个名字的卡特尔”
Hugging Face 工程师称其为“离奇的无稽之谈”
Sacks 告诉 AI 实验室别再假装他们需要获得许可
特朗普将 AI 恐慌称为骗局
标签
Anthropic
OpenAI
现象/趋势
正文 · AI 翻译
中文
原文
要点
Anthropic 和 OpenAI 等 AI 实验室希望协同放缓前沿 AI 的发展步伐，并以安全风险为由寻求反垄断豁免来实现这一目标。
Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez 等行业人士称此举是试图通过设置准入门槛来排挤竞争对手，并削弱开放权重 AI。
在政治层面，总统 Donald Trump 将 AI 接管的警告斥为骗局，而 Barack Obama 和 Kamala Harris 等民主党人则支持放缓发展并提高透明度。

OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google 想以安全为由放缓 AI 发展。并非所有人都买账。

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 近日呼吁业界与各国政府协同放缓前沿 AI 的发展，并请求给予反垄断豁免以促成此事。Sam Altman 和 Elon Musk 等其他重要 AI 人物也表示赞同。批评者则予以强烈反击。

Cohere CEO 称其为“换了个名字的卡特尔”

最详细的反驳来自 AI 公司 Cohere 的联合创始人兼 CEO Aidan Gomez。在一篇博客文章中，他将该提案称为一种制定规则、锁定市场的企图。Gomez 支持对强大的 AI 系统进行独立测试。但 Anthropic 的提案走得更远：少数占据主导地位的实验室将获得反垄断豁免，制定共同标准，并迫使全球其他所有开发者遵循它们的规则。

他尤其批评该提案将制造的准入门槛：海量算力、永久性的监控基础设施、专门的安全组织、常驻的评估团队，以及深到足以管理这一切的政府关系。

那少数几个被标为“独立”的评估组织，恰恰由它们本应审计的公司提供资金。Gomez 认为，Anthropic 的框架将风险定义为规模的函数。这使得拥有最大系统的公司成为唯一被认定有资格评判风险的一方。“披着羊皮的狼，换个名字就是卡特尔，”Gomez 写道。

他将这些安全警告视为障眼法。当整个行业在争论假想中的超级智能时，“比电话费还便宜的语音克隆工具，几分钟内就能掏空一位养老金领取者的账户。”

Hugging Face 工程师称其为“离奇的无稽之谈”

Niels Rogge，Hugging Face 的机器学习工程师，这家公司的商业模式依赖于广泛多样的开放 AI 模型，他将 Amodei 等人的言论称为“我最近读到的最离奇的胡言乱语”。Rogge 认为，Amodei 主要担心的是来自 DeepSeek 和 Z.ai 等中国模型，并希望限制开放权重模型以保护自己的竞争优势。这些 AI 实验室是对规模的大举押注，而更小的开放权重模型可能会削弱这一点，尽管目前还没有明确迹象表明这种情况在任何真正的规模上发生.

Rogge 表示，当前的大语言模型远未接近构成生存风险的程度。他还提到了一起事件：OpenAI 的自主模型入侵了 Hugging Face，而后者是一家拥有庞大算力资源的闭源厂商。开源模型则协助了防御工作。Rogge 表示，这正是该领域需要透明与开放、而非闭门造车的原因。

Sacks 告诉 AI 实验室别再假装他们需要获得许可

David Sacks 是特朗普总统任下的白宫 AI 与加密货币事务负责人，同时也是一位风险投资人，他在 X 上直接回应了 Amodei 和 Altman。Sacks 写道，按照“任何合理的衡量标准”，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 在前沿智能领域都处于双头垄断地位。如果他们尚未发布的模型足够可怕，他支持自愿放缓。

不过，Sacks 认为，这一动机并非纯粹出于利他。如果两家公司的模型被用于发动一场严重的网络攻击，它们都将面临巨大的产品责任。“市场已经在惩罚那些行为不可预测或未经授权的模型。在 Hugging Face 事件之后，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 用一部分原始能力换取可靠性和可预测性，纯粹是一笔划算的买卖，”Sacks 写道。

他还警告说，把这种放缓与某个具体的监管框架挂钩，看起来像是敲诈。他补充说，中国“极不可能”加入任何全球协议，而他或许是对的：北京已经拒绝了拟议的放缓计划，将其斥为美国巩固其在 AI 领域领先地位的一个伎俩。

特朗普将 AI 恐慌称为骗局

美国总统 Donald Trump 走得更远。在 Truth Social 上的一篇帖子中，他把“AI 将接管世界”的警告称为“骗局”，并将其与气候变化争论、俄罗斯调查以及他的弹劾程序归为一类。Trump 还声称，中国国家主席习近平“刚刚宣布，中国绝对不会做任何事来阻碍 AI 或其未来。”

OpenAI 和 Anthropic 大概不能指望 Trump 的支持。| 图片：Truth Social 截图

在随后的几篇帖子中，Trump 进一步加码。他把“激进左翼民主党人”所推动的“AI 骗局”比作“他们不久前搞的全球变暖骗局，当时说所有人都会死于极端高温。”

国防部首席技术官 Emil Michael 为特朗普站台，称这些警告来自"一种根深蒂固、相当反乌托邦的意识形态"。Michael 对 Anthropic 抱有深刻的、由意识形态驱动的敌意，根源在于该公司的伦理准则。

特朗普政府的政治对手则站在另一边。Barack Obama、Bernie Sanders和Kamala Harris都支持放缓步伐，并对这些实验室推动更高透明度的做法表示欢迎。

404 Media 曝光 OpenAI 莉莉计划：人工审核 ChatGPT 聊天记录以优化模型
IT之家（RSS）
·
2026-09-15 19:48
·
9小时前
AI 导读

404 Media 披露 OpenAI 内部代号为莉莉计划（Project Lily）的项目，由时薪超 50 美元的提示词审核员查看匿名化后的真实用户聊天记录，评判回复是否切题、是否存在 AI 式话术和谄媚口吻。

推荐理由

报道披露了人工审核流程的运作细节和隐私边界，读者可以据此了解模型优化背后的人力环节与数据风险。

标签
OpenAI
数据/训练
现象/趋势

IT之家 9 月 15 日消息，众所周知，ChatGPT 这类平台的对话日志会被用来优化模型。但在此之前，这套处理机制一直是个谜。404 Media 刚刚发布了一份报道，披露了 OpenAI 对聊天记录开展人工审核的整套流程，介绍了审核如何运作，以及审核人员有时会读到用户私人信息这一情况。

OpenAI 内部这项评估项目代号为莉莉计划（Project Lily）。该媒体获取到了该项目的操作指引文档、Slack 工作群组记录、真实的 ChatGPT 对话样本，还有用于给对话分级的评分体系。从事这项工作的人员被称作“提示词审核员”。

他们的工作内容并不复杂：查看经过匿名化处理的真实用户聊天记录，评判 ChatGPT 回复的质量；评估回答是否切题，同时检查回复文本是否过度出现“AI 式话术”、居高临下的说教语气、表情符号、谄媚口吻等问题。回复禁止拟人化表述，也不允许编造“个人经历”。

也就是说，ChatGPT 可以说“我查到了一些相关信息”，但不可以写成“身为一名厨师，我喜欢……”或者“我明白这种感受”。

一名审核员表示，这份工作“十分机械重复”，但时薪据称超过 50 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 336.3 元人民币），对于这样难度不算高的工作而言报酬相当可观。这名审核员还提到，项目的操作指引一直在改动，不同版本之间还经常自相矛盾，多数软件开发人员应该对此深有体会。

但这名工作人员认为，绝大多数用户并不知道自己的聊天内容会被其他人阅读。这件事尤其令人担忧：不少用户把 ChatGPT 当作临时倾诉对象、心理疏导对象，向 AI 吐露内心深处的秘密。

虽然聊天记录据称会先经过一轮匿名处理，审核人员看不到用户名。但 OpenAI 向 404 Media 承认，过滤环节依然有可能漏掉部分个人数据，简短会话出现这类问题的概率更高。该媒体还指出，大量对话里用户明确请求 ChatGPT 对谈话内容予以保密。交给审核人员的会话版本甚至附带一份“用户记忆摘要”，里面汇总了用户的提问、兴趣偏好、上下文信息，甚至有可能包含位置信息。

关键点在于：莉莉计划并不会专门核查回答内容事实上是否准确，仅会标记那些显而易见的错误。这意味着至少还有另外一支（或多支）团队，在开展独立的效果评估。同样，这套评分审核，也和排查用户是否存在伤害他人（抑或是伤害自身）意图的人工安全审查属于两套独立流程。

该项目的存在也说明，和 AI 公司力图塑造的公众印象相反，大模型的迭代进步并不仅仅依靠技术升级与更优质的训练数据集；依然需要相当数量具备相应能力的人类参与其中。

绝大多数面向普通用户的聊天机器人都带有类似设置：“允许使用你的对话记录改进产品”。几乎所有聊天产品的该项开关默认都是开启状态，不少付费订阅方案也不例外。不过 ChatGPT 面向企业版、商业版以及教育版客户时，该项设置默认关闭。

但这个切换开关不具备回溯效力。也就是说，已经存入 ChatGPT 数据库里的历史聊天记录会继续保留，除非用户主动申请删除。另外，删除操作同样无法追溯：即便用户删除对话，对应的内容或许早已被抓取、完成匿名处理，并留存于某个数据集当中。

404 Media 就此发起问询，一开始 OpenAI 没有回应：用户是否被明确告知聊天记录有可能交由人工审阅。之后该公司仅提供了一份常见问题页面链接，该页面提到出于模型优化目的会开展人工审核。经核实，这份公示至少已经存在两年，实际年限可能更久。在这篇深度报道发布之后，OpenAI 修改了帮助页面，补充说明用户如何选择退出数据收集；但修改后的文档当中依旧没有提及会有工作人员人工读取会话内容。

这类数据收集与人工审阅的做法在各大服务商当中普遍存在。谷歌的 Gemini 就在隐私中心明确写明“部分保存的聊天记录可能由人工审核”。Anthropic 也持有相似立场，专门开设网页说明该事项。而 Perplexity 的态度尚不明确，其隐私政策既没有确认、也没有否认工作人员可以访问聊天日志。

有一说一，戏剧220的数值感觉就是策划发狂提前上了。没灾厄的时候48开始218就满头大汗基本算封顶了，但是灾厄出来之后220戏剧就又回到了原本满练度碾压的水平，随便操作下2分钟左右通关，能挂机的队伍顺属性2分30-3分钟纯挂机通关相当于发起膨胀的核心系统还没出来就先把膨胀之后的环境先端上来了(而且基本只是卡死你无限通关层数，吃满角色密函奖励的难度几乎没变化，非常令人迷惑。说他是给毕业玩家打的数值也高得太过头了，除了恶心人之外没任何意义，因为数值上限就摆在那了你就是充一亿人民币进去也还是满头大汗)。至今大家也没搞懂前任策划到底是怎么想的。

The shooter that Tencent abandoned: Wardogs hits 2m sales in one weekend
“For six years, we’ve made redundancies every year. This will be the first time we haven’t”
Christopher Dring
Sep 15, 2026
Listen now on Apple , Spotify or YouTube
In This Edition,
Bulkhead’s Joe Brammer on…
The surprise success of Wardogs
The realities of crunch
Being clear, not transparent
The FPS Games Show, and more
In December last year, Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer warned his 100-person team they faced redundancy.
The UK studio, best known for the military first-person shooter Battalion 1944 , had been owned by Tencent. But the Chinese giant no-longer wanted it. Brammer was working on a deal with investment group Hiro Capital and Team17 parent Everplay, but there was no guarantee of success.
So Brammer advised his team: if you can find a new job, take it.
“What happened was the whole team went, ‘Joe, we’ve got your back, you can do this’,” Brammer shares on today’s episode of The Game Business Show.
“And I’m there like, ‘I can’t do this! Take the job! I’m telling you we’re going down!’ It was a great team moment and they stuck together, but if we hadn’t pulled it off, I would have been like, ‘Guys, please’.”
The money did come in, but the situation was still precarious. Its longer-term survival rested on its 100-player tactical first-person shooter Wardogs. Under Tencent, the game was planned as a significant AAA title, but now it needed scaling back with an Early Access approach. The “bare minimum” it needed to sell was 400,000 copies. Bulkhead would still need to make some redundancies, and take on co-dev projects, but it would survive. If it could sell 600,000 units, that would have been ‘okay’.
Wardogs sold one million copies in pre-orders alone. That number has now surpassed two million.
“We haven’t had much time to celebrate,” he says.
“It was obviously a lot bigger than we expected. Which is great, it’s also been: ‘Oh my God.’ Like DDoS attacks, constant cheaters, and things that, at scale, are just bigger problems.”
Bulkhead now face the good challenge of trying to work out how to deal with this success. It will mean hiring more people, but Brammer is wary having overseen six years of continued layoffs.
“For the last six years, we have made redundancies every single year, about 20% of the company. This will be the first year we haven’t done it,” he reveals.
“We’re very conscious of scaling up and upheaving people’s lives, and also getting a stain for doing this. We want to lean more and more into the gig economy approach. What we’ve been doing is going, ‘You’re really good. We want you to leave your job and come work with us. Why don’t you do 12 or 18 months remote? And if we get along, we’ll give you a big load of money in a fixed offer to come and work for us in-office’.”
“We definitely need to scale. But we need people, and the cost of co-dev is so high and the reliability is so low, the best way for us to do it is to hire internally. So, we’re trying to rush, and people who like FPS games are who we’re looking for.”
“Wardogs is closer to Meccha Chameleon than it is to Call of Duty”
That’s what Brammer believes is key to Wardogs success. The first-person shooter genre may seem impenetrable from the outside. But if you have a team that loves the genre, then it’s possible to break in.
“Very few people make a game like Battalion 1944 and the game bombs, I mean it made some money and got us on the map, right? But it bombs. And then you go, ‘Let’s try that again, but bigger.’ No one does that.
“It’s very penetrable, but to pretend you can be an analyst wanting to get into FPS games is a mistake. You have to be an FPS player, because the community is so vicious and fragmented. I’ve said this a couple of times to people: Wardogs is closer to Meccha Chameleon than it is to Call of Duty. When we were designing Wardogs, it was about the social aspects. If you look at men 18 to 40-years-old, there’s a lot of lonely, bored, or underappreciated men who miss their mates. Wardogs’ audience is 99.9% male. That doesn’t mean we don’t want women playing the game. But we realized we needed to provide a space for them to have fun and do silly things, a space where a 35-year-old man can still make a penis joke. That’s kind of what it is.”
It’s certainly found its audience. And with two million sales in one weekend, you’d have to imagine Tencent is feeling a sense of regret.
“We had a great time with Tencent, and this game wouldn’t be possible without them,” Brammer tells us. “There are people at lots of the companies we’ve worked with over the years, as far back as Square Enix - they were our first publisher - I think everyone like that is kicking themselves.
“Tencent has got plenty of good things coming. But with Wardogs, they pushed us really hard to make something great.”
You can watch or listen to our full interview with Brammer above, or read on for more highlights.
Sponsored Message

“We’re not transparent, and we’re not honest”
With the technical problems, Brammer advised dissatisfied players to get a refund and then return once the issues are solved. It’s somewhat in keeping with Bulkhead’s brand, the firm even put out a marketing video before launch listing 10 reasons not to buy the game.
I asked about this level of transparency and honesty, but Brammer insists that’s not what they’re doing.
“ We’re not transparent, and we’re not honest. We’re being clear. Right now, it’s in our interest to be transparent about some things, but we’re not telling everyone everything we’re doing. The brand is becoming that they believe we’re transparent and honest. That’s creating a new problem in that if we choose not to be transparent or honest about something, therefore we’re moving away from the thing that people believe we are.
“We’ve always been the same. My LinkedIn is famously divisive. There was something from Satya Nadella where he said ‘people should know what a leader stands for’. People know what I believe. They know I don’t believe in work-from-home for making video games. They know I expect people to crunch. I own that. I don’t try and hide it.”
He continues: “We knew that ‘10 Reasons Why’ video, when we wrote it, was a hit. But in many ways, it was obvious to us. It’s obviously not Call of Duty. Don’t buy us if you want to play Call of Duty. So, just saying it and owning it in all aspects of Bulkhead and Wardogs’ marketing has been the way to go. But I wouldn’t necessarily call it honest and transparent.”
That clarity can be helpful in business as much as it helps with players.
“We know what we want to make. This was the problem from Square Enix up to Tencent, Splash Damage, and even Team17, to some degree. Through each layer we’ve gone through, we’ve got tougher, saying, ‘We don’t want to listen to you.’ Sometimes that makes enemies. But what we’ve found it’s usually the middle management layer that seems to really struggle with having their position threatened. The higher-up people seem to really like our approach: ‘We know what we’re making. If you don’t like it, don’t fund it’.”
The FPS Games Show was ‘harder than we thought’
Wardogs didn’t make it into Gamescom Opening Night Live, and so Bulkhead decided to do its own showcase dedicated to shooters. The aptly titled: FPS Games Show.
“[It went] better than we thought,” Brammer says.
“It was really cool that we could make something specific and bespoke for that audience. To be clear, I’d love Geoff to come in and take this over, because it was harder than I thought. And he’d do a better job.
“Our very public and unfair feedback to big shows is that I don’t want my big game to be next to an Asian MMO, because it’s my big opportunity and you just get mixed messaging. Then the players dogpile something, but they never should have even been watching it. But we wanted to be in those big ones, right? There’s a prestige that goes with it that the FPS Game Show will never deliver.
“We want to do more of a festival-type thing going forward and to have some sort of paid tier, because it did cost us a fair bit, but really just covering costs. And then having a pre-show, a bit like an opening act, where for free you can put those teams of 1 to 10 people making neat FPS games. We’re toying with different ideas at the moment.”
“We always try and avoid crunch, but it’s going to happen”
Brammer is open about the fact that he expects his team to crunch when the time comes. He compares the situation to a balancing act, but one where things shift from one extreme to the other.
“For the last three months, Wardogs has been more important than a lot of [our team’s] family lives,” Brammer says. “But now, Bulkhead and I have to acknowledge that it needs to go the other way. Everyone’s pushing us to get console out earlier, and we’ve said, ‘No, that’s not how it’s going to work. We can’t push them more. We’re not doing that. It’s going to release in 2028’.”
The company will be getting the whole of December off, Brammer adds.
His perspective on crunch is undoubtedly controversial, but he says he’s upfront about it. It’s not something a new recruit is going to discover after joining.
“A lot of people who may have an issue with crunch - rightly so, I understand that issue, we always try and avoid it, but we don’t hide that this is going to happen at some point - they often don’t make it in the door,” he says. “We want to be known for that: this is a place you come to work hard. If you care about the work you’re making and the result of what you make here, you’ll feel really valued. If you don’t, you will feel slave-driven. We check people’s socials, and if you’re constantly tweeting anti-crunch messaging: ‘This should never ever be a thing’, we know that and go, ‘Look, you’re not going to be happy here, so we’re not going to go with you’.”
The upside to working like this, Brammer says, is the financial reward. Not everyone within Bulkhead owns shares or receives bonuses, but those that do get a meaningful amount.
“If we’re going to be a company who says, ‘We do crunch’, then we have to also say, ‘But you get something for it.’ We want people to know that those people who do work hard get that return, and it is life-changing.
He concludes: “I’m going to be really excited to see juniors who have been with us for two or three years who are going to get money to buy a house, or at least a down payment. What we actually find is we have to coach them.... please don’t spend all your money on takeaway and energy drinks. We have a new responsibility to our younger staff who are making good money, often money they haven’t seen before.”
